chapter: The 1940s: small groups, Teddy Wilson and Ethel Waters
title: Teddy Wilson's sextet and V-Discs
summary: Thomas spent about a year in Teddy Wilson's sextet at Cafe Society, with Benny Morton, Edmond Hall and Sid Catlett, and recorded V-Discs during the Petrillo recording ban.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And then there's the next thing Teddy Wilson.
Yeah, with Teddy and a tremendous musician.
Oh, you weren't in the big band?
Because he had a big band around this time, too.
Yeah, well, Teddy -- I might have gotten the years mixed up -- no, that's a small band.
You did this for about a year with Teddy, didn't you, Baby?

Oh, yeah. There was Teddy, of course. ... Benny Morton is on this side, there's Joe Thomas, trumpet player and Edmond me, Edward Hall, Sidney Catlett and Johnny Wilson. And, that was during the time of a record strike. Petrillo had called a record strike and we couldn't record at all. But, we did some things for the overseas things that you do.
The overseas things that you do.
We did some V Discs and out of that idea I met some tremendous people that heard, they said I heard you in the fox holes, you know. That was a tremendous band.
